featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited LensKart one day ago for an eye test, which was conducted via video call. This is not accurate because a physical, in‑person eye check by a doctor is very different from a video call; the video‑call doctor cannot examine the eyes properly.
Just two days before that visit, my old glasses were lost. My correct prescription was right eye −15 and left eye −1, but I had no glasses at that time. I only had an old pair of glasses with right eye −8 and left eye −1. LensKart used this incorrect old prescription to prepare my new glasses, and I was given lenses based on the wrong power. If I had worn those glasses regularly, my eyesight could have become worse or even damaged.
Later I visited another store, where my actual prescription was checked again. There, my power was found to be right eye −15 and left eye −2, which is correct. This proves that LensKart gave me the wrong lenses based on an outdated and incorrect prescription.
I am very concerned because this is not just about money; it is about people’s eyes and health. Someone’s eyesight could be seriously harmed if this kind of mistake happens again. I therefore request LensKart to take strict action to prevent such errors in the future, and to improve their eye‑test process so that every customer’s eyes are checked properly and safely don't refer to lanskard
